chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission (of a slave) for the believer after death.
Nor is there a gift (donation) after death.
Nor is there charity after death.
Except for what he has bequeathed.
ai.seo_question: What acts of a believer do not take effect after death according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that voluntary acts like freeing a slave or giving charity are revocable during life but require a specific bequest (*wasiyyah*) to take effect posthumously. This ruling distinguishes between general charity (*sadaqah*) and testamentary gifts, establishing that the deceased’s estate is bound by the will to execute these specific obligations. It underscores the Shia legal principle that posthumous charitable acts are not automatic but depend on the explicit instruction left in the will.
